back: Government by the people, directly or through representatives chosen in free and fair elections (Greek demos = people, kratos = rule).
The right of every adult citizen to vote; in Zimbabwe from age 18.
Citizens decide for themselves, e.g. in a referendum.
Citizens elect representatives (MPs, councillors, a president) to decide for them.
Parliamentary: Prime Minister from parliament, removable by no confidence (Zimbabwe 1980-87). Presidential: separately elected executive President (Zimbabwe since 1987).
Participation, free and fair elections, rule of law, separation of powers, accountability, freedom of expression (also minority rights and human rights).

front: When was the Zimbabwe Electoral Commission established?
Give four ways government has promoted democracy in Zimbabwe.
back: Universal suffrage and regular elections; referendums; independent commissions; devolution and reserved seats for women (and the 2013 Declaration of Rights).

front: What criticisms have been made of democracy in Zimbabwe?
back: Disputed elections, violence in some campaigns (especially 2008), restrictive laws such as POSA (2002) and questions about institutional independence.
